Evelyn (docs): Pushed a small PR that combines proxy/PAC examples, offline package repo steps, and CA verification for private installs. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1402 :memo:
Harun (security): Nice. Customers often get tripped up by proxy chaining + apt/yum metadata verification. Can you add a signed-repo example and show how to verify a GPG key before import?
Evelyn (docs): Yep. I'll include both apt (deb) and rpm examples plus a minimal gpg verify step. Draft snippet (keeps code block paste-friendly):
```
# add host override for sealed environments
sudo sh -c 'echo "<control-ip> control.redwood.example" >> /etc/hosts'
# probe proxy chain (PAC or explicit) - curl via proxy
curl -I -x http://<proxy-host>:3128 https://control.redwood.example/health
# add offline apt repo (deb) example
sudo mkdir -p /opt/redwood-offline && cp <mirror-path>/*.deb /opt/redwood-offline/
cd /opt/redwood-offline && dpkg-scanpackages . /dev/null | gzip -9c > Packages.gz
# rpm repo example
createrepo /opt/redwood-offline-rpm
# checksum + verify bundle
sha256sum <bundle-name>.tar.gz > <bundle-name>.sha256
sha256sum -c <bundle-name>.sha256
# verify repo GPG key (optional)
curl -sSL https://<key-server>/<repo-key>.gpg | gpg --dearmor > /usr/share/keyrings/<repo-key>.gpg
```
Mina (eng-infra): For proxies add a short note about CONNECT semantics: some proxies block CONNECT to non-443 ports which breaks HSM mgmt traffic. Recommend agent tunnel over 443 or put HSM mgmt behind a bastion.
Evelyn (docs): Good point. I'll add a short paragraph about proxy CONNECT limits and an example `curl --proxy` note for HTTPS healthchecks.
Diego (installer): For the installer: we accept `--offline-repo-path` and a `--signed-repo-key` flag. If you document the expected keyring path (`/usr/share/keyrings/<repo-key>.gpg`) that's helpful so I can wire auto-import. Also mention permissions and owner (redwood:root 0640).
Harun (security): Also add instructions for verifying detached signatures if customers sign the tarball with an HSM-backed key: `gpg --verify <bundle>.sig <bundle>` and a fallback `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify <pubkey.pem> -signature <bundle>.sig <bundle>`. Call out that HSM operations are customer-managed.
Evelyn (docs): Added both GPG and openssl detached-sign examples in prose, plus a tiny troubleshooting line for checksum mismatch.
Mina (eng-infra): Small nit: for the apt example include `apt-ftparchive` vs `dpkg-scanpackages` depending on distro tooling; maybe link to our offline repo guide anchor. Also recommend `apt-get update` against the local file:// repo to validate metadata.
Evelyn (docs): Will do. Replaced `dpkg-scanpackages` with a note listing both tools and added `sudo apt-get update -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist="sources.list.d/redwood.list"` example.
ops-bot: docs staging build OK (2026-03-25-1400) :white_check_mark:
Diego (installer): I'll add a postinstall smoke test to validate the GPG key import and run `apt-get update` or `yum makecache` if `--offline-repo-path` is used. Filing issue after merge: https://github.com/redwood-inference/installer/issues/523
Evelyn (docs): Thanks all — I'll push the final small edits (link anchors, proxy caveats, keyring path) and mark PR ready for review. Closing after merge. :thumbsup:
